insights.claim: The spark-operator-module implements the ODH PlatformObject interface, enabling standardized lifecycle management by the ODH Operator through a singleton SparkOperator CR with condition reporting and management state control.
insights.reasoning: The SparkOperator type explicitly asserts var _ common.PlatformObject = &SparkOperator{} and embeds ManagementSpec, Status, and ComponentReleaseStatus from odh-platform-utilities. This compile-time check proves the platform integration contract is enforced, not optional.

insights.claim: The operator dynamically reads the OpenShift APIServer TLS profile at startup and falls back to TLS 1.2 with Intermediate cipher suites, aligning webhook TLS configuration with cluster-wide security policy.
insights.reasoning: FetchTLSProfile reads config.openshift.io/v1/APIServer and translates its tlsSecurityProfile into Go crypto/tls cipher suites. The Intermediate fallback uses only FIPS-compatible ECDHE ciphers. This pattern ensures the operator respects platform-level TLS hardening without manual per-component configuration.

insights.claim: Webhook TLS certificates are managed through two independent strategies: an internal self-signed provider in the core operator and cert-manager CRs provisioned by the module controller, creating a potential dual-provisioning overlap.
insights.reasoning: The core operator has RBAC to create/update the spark-operator-webhook-certs Secret directly (internal provider), while the module controller has RBAC for cert-manager.io certificates and issuers. Both paths target the same webhook TLS endpoint, which could cause certificate rotation conflicts if both are active simultaneously.
